messages.content: What's project is "Adriel" working on? exclude any that are completed?

function.name: get_adriel_projects
function.description: Retrieve a list of projects that are associated with Adriel, including their current status and estimated completion dates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user Adriel.

include_completed.description: A flag to determine whether to include completed projects in the list.

status_filter.description: Filter projects by status, such as 'active', 'paused', or 'completed'.

function.name: get_detail_adriel_projects
function.description: Retrieve detailed information about projects that Adriel is or has been involved in, including project status and participation role. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

project_name.description: The unique name of the project for which details are to be fetched.

include_archived.description: A flag to determine whether to include projects that are archived. Defaults to false.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What's project is 'Adriel' working on? exclude any that are completed?" They want to know what project(s) Adriel is working on, excluding completed ones.

We have a function get_adriel_projects that can retrieve a list of projects associated with Adriel, including status and estimated completion dates. It accepts parameters: user_id (string), include_completed (boolean, default false), status_filter ("active"|"paused"|"completed", default active). We need to call this function. But we don't have Adriel's user ID. The user didn't provide it. We might ask for the user ID. Or maybe we can assume we have some mapping from name to ID. But we can't guess. So we should ask the user for the unique identifier of Adriel. The question: "What's project is 'Adriel' working on? exclude any that are completed?" We could interpret that they want all projects that Adriel is currently working on, i.e., active or paused but not completed. The function get_adriel_projects allows us to filter by status_filter. If we set status_filter to "active", we will only get active projects. That excludes paused and completed. But if we want both active and paused, we would need to call twice or adjust logic. The user says "exclude any that are completed". So we want all non-completed projects. That includes active and paused. The function doesn't support filtering out completed while including both active and paused. But we can call with status_filter="active" to get active ones. But that excludes paused. Alternatively, we can call with include_completed=false and no status_filter, which defaults to active. Actually default status_filter is active. So we cannot get paused unless we specify status_filter=paused. There's no option to get both active and paused at once. So we might need to call twice: one for active, one for paused. But the user just wants to know what project is Adriel working on. Maybe they expect a single project. But we can't guarantee there's only one. We can ask for user ID first. Then we can call get_adriel_projects with include_completed=false and status_filter="active" to get active projects. That will give us active ones. If there are none, we can also check paused. But let's start by asking for Adriel's user ID.
